questions.q: Why can a tree model not follow a strong upward trend into the future?
options: Trees predict averages of training targets, so they cannot go above the training range
why: Correct: leaves hold values seen in training.
Trees use lag features well.
Trees do not need scaled inputs.

questions.q: Which objective suits daily sales with many zeros and a long right tail?
why: Squared error chases the rare large values and can predict negatives.
Correct: they model non-negative skewed counts.
The median of mostly zeros is zero, which is not helpful for planning.
Correct: pinball loss with level 0.9.
Absolute error gives the median.
Squared error gives the mean.

questions.q: Your gradient boosting model uses a random 20% of the training rows for early stopping. What is the problem?
options: Validation rows are mixed in time with training rows, so the validation score is too good
Early stopping cannot be used with trees
why: It leaks neighbouring days into validation.
Correct: use the newest part of the training period.
It can be used, with a time-ordered validation set.

questions.q: The trend makes test values higher than any training value. You want to keep a tree model. What is a good fix?
options: Predict y(t) − y(t−7) and add the lag back
why: Correct: the change stays in the training range.
More trees cannot create values outside the range.
Shuffling leaks the future.

questions.q: Select all statements that are true about feature importance.
options: Correlated features can share importance and each look small
A dominant feature with a perfect score is a leakage warning
Permutation importance on out-of-time data is more reliable than training-set gain
why: Yes.
Yes. Look for a target-like feature.
No. It only shows what the model used.
Yes. It measures the loss in out-of-time error.

questions.q: You compare a complex LightGBM with MAE 9.8 to seasonal naive MAE 9.5 on the same folds. What is your conclusion?
options: LightGBM is better because it is more advanced
LightGBM adds no value yet; check features, objective and trend handling
why: Complexity does not count. Only the score on the same folds counts.
Correct: the baseline is better. Improve the model or keep the baseline.
The baseline is simple and usually correct.
